en: The Sūtra on the Efficacious Dharma of the Six-Syllable Mantra of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
Homage to the Honored One, the Benefactor of All, the Youthful Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
The mantra is: *Aṃ ba ki ta na ma*. Regarding this Mañjuśrī...
I shall now explain the ritual method for the efficacy of the six-syllable mantra of the Bodhisattva.
If there is anyone who recites this mantra seven times every day, [they shall obtain its benefits].
One's determined sinful karma will certainly be eradicated.
If there is anyone who can recite this mantra one hundred and eight times every day,
at the time of that person's death, they will...
One will see Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva appearing before them.
If there is anyone who receives and maintains this dhāraṇī and attains success in the Dharma,
they should first eat vegetables or consume milk gruel.
He would eat either a gruel of barley seeds,
or parched barley flour, or subsist on almsfood;
every day at dawn, at midday, and at sunset— these three times— he bathed.
Don a separate set of clean robes and recite this mantra six hundred thousand times; the rite will then be accomplished.
Thereafter, do not cut the threads on the loom.
The painters, having received the eight precepts,
used no glue to depict Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva in the form of one seated upon a lotus flower while preaching the Dharma.
Fully endowed with all ornaments,
appearing in the form of a youth with a celestial robe draped over the left shoulder;
to the right, one should paint the noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Seated upon a lotus throne and holding a fly-whisk in his hand,
one should paint the noble Bodhisattva Samantabhadra to his left;
above the image, both sides of the void should be depicted.
From within the clouds, a mantra-adept (vidyādhara) emerges, holding a flower garland in his hand.
Below the painted image, one should depict a mantra-holding person holding an incense burner,
gazing up in reverence at Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
The four sides of the image should all be fashioned with mountain peaks.
Beneath the Bodhisattva’s seat,
one should fashion a flower pond filled with lotuses.
Thereafter, facing west before the stūpa of the śarīra,
having arranged an extensive array of offerings,
one should burn lamps with ghee.
Take one thousand and eight *jāti* flowers;
recite the mantra once over each flower and scatter them before the face of the image.
Immediately a sound will emerge, and you shall hear a subtle and wondrous voice, or the image may tremble.
When one hears wondrous sounds, they shall find them to their heart's content;
when the staff moves, one shall achieve victory in all debates and disputes,
and shall thoroughly master all worldly teachings and discourses.
All sentient beings love and delight in this;
if one does not accomplish this dharma,
all other undertakings will not be successful.
Furthermore, there is another method: take a piece of agarwood eight finger-widths long, regardless of its thickness or width, and coat it with *suhagandha* (stacte) oil.
Recite the mantra once over each piece while they are held in a smokeless fire of *khadira* wood charcoal.
If one burns [the incense] from the first watch of the night until the appearance of the dawn light,
one will immediately see Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva come in person before the mantra-practitioner and fulfill all requests according to their wishes.
With the sole exception of sexual desire,
one should also burn sandalwood incense before the sacred pillar day and night without interruption while reciting this mantra.
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva came in person and expounded the most profound Dharma for them; they all attained resolute understanding,
were forever freed from all illnesses, and attained mastery.
One will attain entry into the stages of a bodhisattva.
Furthermore, as for the method: carve a lotus flower six finger-widths long from red sandalwood;
then, grind red sandalwood powder with water.
Anoint it and recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times.
On the night of the fifteenth day, when the moon is full, take flowers and leaves before the wooden tablet; holding the leaves and flowers in both hands, recite the mantra.
When light emerges from the crown of his head, one should take that flower;
it will cause that person to attain a physical form as dignified and beautiful as that of a sixteen-year-old,
with golden radiance surpassing that of a thousand suns.
His majestic radiance will be like that of a celestial youth, and he will achieve all accomplishments.
All mantra-adepts (vidyādhara) will revere him, and his lifespan will last for one kalpa.
At the end of that kalpa, he will be reborn in the world of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
Furthermore, there is another method: during a lunar eclipse,
one should take the root of white kanda (gloriosa superba) and [process it] with the dung of a cow, milk, curd, and ghee.
Next, wash the root of *achyranthes aspera* with the five-fold water.

Having washed it, place it beneath a *pippala* leaf and fruit; arrange four leaves upon it and place three leaves on top. Recite the mantra until smoke issues forth, or warmth arises, or flames emerge.
If it is the time when warmth arises,
one will gain the joy of sentient beings and be victorious over all disputations.
If smoke issues forth, [the same results follow].
Those who attain the lifespan of Anāgāmin live for ten thousand years;
if the flames of fire emerge, they ascend to Ākāśa and live for one great kalpa.
Furthermore, there is another method:
take a yellow cow that has a calf, churn its milk and curd to extract the ghee, and place it in a vessel of refined copper.
Cover it with seven leaves of *piṇḍītaka* and recite the mantra over it.
When the three matters, such as the smoke and so forth, have been accomplished as described above,
one should then consume this ghee—
either the "Much-Hearing" (Bahuśruta) variety or the "Andhara" variety.
Alternatively, one may ascend to Ākāśa.
Furthermore, there is a method: take a *puṇḍarīka* flower during a lunar eclipse, place it within the sun, and recite this mantra while holding it.
When the seed is ready to be moved,
take three types of copper to fashion beads with holes;
insert the seed into the holes of the beads and hold it within them.
Then Andhalī opened her mouth, and he saw it.
Furthermore, there is a method: take a nail and hold it in the mouth with incense.
Having recited this mantra six hundred thousand times, whatever one seeks will be obtained in accordance with the words spoken to others.
Furthermore, there is another method: consume milk, barley grains, or barley flour.
If one recites the mantra one million two hundred thousand times,
one will attain the status of a mantra-siddha (mantra-rishi).
Furthermore, according to another method, when begging for alms, one must not speak.
If one completes one hundred thousand recitations, one will attain the stage of Anutattva.
If one recites the mantra for a full koṭi,
one will then behold the noble Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva preaching the Dharma in this manner.
It will certainly cause one to enter the assembly of Great Bodhisattvas who are in their final birth before Buddhahood (Ekajātipratibaddha).
If one recites this mantra regularly,
all who receive its benefit shall achieve fulfillment.
Furthermore, there is another method: take agallochum incense and grind it into a powder.
Mix it with clarified butter to form pills the size of small jujubes, making one hundred thousand pills in total.
Recite the mantra over each one once.
Burn them completely in the fire;
this will yield one hundred thousand gold coins.
Furthermore, there is another method: at a great river flowing into the sea, take ten thousand lotus flowers and recite the mantra over each one once;
then cast them into the river until they are all exhausted.
It is like seeing a treasure trove of jewels as numerous as those lotuses;
having found that treasury, one enjoys its contents inexhaustibly.
Furthermore, as for the ritual involving sesame seeds, they should be mixed with curd and ghee.
Take a pinch [of the substance] and recite the mantra over it once for each pinch.
Place them in the fire until one hundred thousand recitations have been completed;
that person will obtain wealth.
One is able to bestow all things.
Furthermore, according to the rite, one should take *goyakṣanī* soil that has not yet fallen to the ground to construct an altar.
One should scatter various flowers upon it and sit there.
Recite the mantra one thousand and eight times every day,
and then read Mahāyāna sūtras.
Upon reaching the completion of one month, one will attain wisdom and sagacity.
Furthermore, there is a method: take ox-gallstone and recite the mantra over it one thousand and eight times, then smear it upon the forehead;
all sentient beings who see this will rejoice.
Recite the mantra seven times over the hair on the crown of the head and bind it there.
No evil person will be able to cause harm.
Furthermore, there is a method: take ten thousand *jīmūta* fruits and recite the mantra over each one once.
Place it within fire until it is completely consumed;
all illnesses will thereby be cured and healed.
*The One-Scroll Dharma of the Six-Syllable Mantra of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva*, based on the manuscript from Kōyasan Kōzanji.
It was transcribed on the stone steps of the Yihui Hall at Dabao’en Temple in Northern Luoyang.
The *Lubajialu* states:
"The *Six-Syllable Divine Mantra Sūtra*, one fascicle."
The commentary states: "Some call it the *Ṣaḍakṣarīdhāraṇīsūtra*.
[The *Zhenyuan* catalog] lacks the entry for the *Brahmaviśeṣacinti*."
The commentary also refers to it as the "Method of the Six-Syllable Mantra.
Its title reads: "The Method of the Efficacy of the Six Syllables of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
[End of] Fascicle Two. *Bok-sō-ji*.
Citing this sutra.
On the eighth day of the second month in the year of Mingwu Wusih (1845), written by Ciren of Dongwu under Zhijilun. The eighth month of the second year of the Xianghe era.
At the request of the Master Jirin, I have transcribed this; it has been collated and verified by Chōtō and others of Jishin-in on this mountain.
I have further revised and corrected it for the sake of the public and for circulation throughout the world.

Recorded by the śramaṇa Kaidō of the Shōjiji Aranya at Chōkōzan on the first day of the fourth month in the third year of Kyōwa, the *Kaihēi* (癸亥) year. Completed with one proofreading and additions by Jison.
